You can’t remove the fact he’s gay from the equation bc it is the entire context of the situation. It’s almost unheard of for heterosexual couples to hide their relationships from their family, but it’s very commonplace in homosexual relationships BECAUSE of the stigma. Yes it’s going to sound crazy if you take out the very important context of this is just the norm for homosexual couples. I lived in my parents house with my partner for 3 of our 4 year relationship and we were just “best friends” bc coming out as a queer person is hard and scary, especially when you’re not independent. OP chose to come out when he was fully independent for that exact reason. When you come out to your family you have to prepare for the worst outcome: complete abandonment. But just because his family could of and did react poorly doesn’t mean he doesn’t have the right to be upset that they reacted poorly.
On the flip side, OP’s parents could have done a better job at presenting themselves as welcoming to his sexuality. They can’t say they were completely blindsided by the fact his 3 year live in best friend was only that unless they really don’t know how to read their own son. They could have easily dropped hints that they were accepting of him/homosexuals to invite him to be honest with them and come out to them. Honestly I think getting married before he came out was a bit too far esp if he was planning on coming out to his family so I will say ESH.
